newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ankara wants allied protection for Iraq Turkomans.
newsitem.headline: Ankara wants allied protection for Iraq Turkomans.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller on Saturday demanded in her latest meeting with the U.S. ambassador over Iraq that Western protection be given to ethnic Turks in rebel northern Iraq.

"Under Operation Provide Comfort it was envisaged that Kurdish citizens in northern Iraq be be protected. We want the Turkomans to be taken within this framework of protection," Ciller told reporters after her meeting with ambassador Marc Grossman.
"The Turkomans are being harmed. They are suffering loss of life and loss of property," Ciller said.

Representatives of the Turkomans, a Turkic community of around two million of whom 200,000 live in northern Iraq, have complained that Iraqi soldiers were arresting and killing some Turkomans after they stormed the main northern city of Arbil in a joint attack with an Iraqi Kurdish faction a week ago.
Ciller said the Turkomans should have more of a say in what goes on in northern Iraq.
"The contribution of the Turkomans in the resolution of issues has become a necessity," she said.

Saturday's session was at least the third meeting between Ciller and Grossman this week and took place amid indications that Turkey would mount a strike against the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels across the border.

Turkish troops have been massing on the border with northern Iraq in apparent readiness to push against the PKK, but military officials would not confirm or deny Turkish press reports that the military had already mounted some cross-border attacks.

The United States said on Thursday it did not object to a Turkish plan to establish a three to six mile (five to 10 km) wide security zone in northern Iraq after Ankara said it would be temporary and not involve the stationing of Turkish troops.

Turkey says the PKK has increased activity in the volatile border region since Baghdad intervened in fighting between Iraqi Kurd rebels in northern Iraq and Washington fired cruise missiles at targets in southern Iraqi in retaliation.
